correctness.rationale: The greedy binary arch decomposition consists of words a^m opposite(a) and a residual unary/empty suffix. The exact earliest-match condition for a shortest absent subsequence gives a two-coordinate transfer: if m=1 the own-initial-letter count propagates, and if m>=2 that coordinate vanishes; the opposite-initial-letter count equals the sum of suffix coordinates. Summing all arches gives a symmetric 2x2 transfer with eigenvector (1,1), eigenvalue u*z^2*(3-z)/(1-z), and residual vector (1,1)/(1-z); formal geometric inversion proves H exactly. Coefficient extraction and singularity analysis yield the finite sum, recurrence, and positive exponential mean. Independently generated all 2047 words n<=10 and brute enumerated subsequences, matching the bivariate coefficients and scalar totals. Empty/unary ambient alphabet convention retained.
residual_risks: Finite checks corroborate; the formal transfer proves arbitrary n. Exponential mean is not typical-value concentration.
